objectives.how: Read all 794 lines of RFC 0011 v1.3 from disk (sha1 5e40aa5f86f04e54a593f86cc5afba5d74bcc9a7) in this lens: normative language and requirement quality. Checked each line against RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 (both read in the browser on 2026-11-16) and against the requirement characteristics named in OBJ-2. Sections 3 and 6 to 7 carry nearly all defects; sections 4, 5, 8 to 10 and appendix A are informative and yielded none in this lens beyond line 42. Every quoted RFC line in the observations was copied from disk by a script that also checked each old text occurs exactly once on its stated line.

deliverables.text: This AAR: one observation and one proposal (old -> new) per defect

objectives.text: Review RFC 0011 v1.3 line by line for normative language and requirement quality: RFC 2119 as clarified by RFC 8174 (keywords in uppercase only where normative; a lowercase must, should or may in a normative clause is ambiguous); every MUST and MUST NOT names its actor and can be verified by a test or an inspection; every SHOULD says or implies when departing from it is acceptable; every requirement is singular (one obligation), unambiguous and free of vague terms (for example short, large, well within); passive voice that hides who acts; and the requirement characteristics of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 (necessary, unambiguous, complete, singular, feasible, verifiable, correct, consistent). Report each defect with the RFC line and the exact replacement text.
objectives.how: Each defect is an observation (line, characteristic or rule violated, verbatim RFC text) with a matching proposal whose `what` is 'line <n>: <old> -> <new>'. Checks applied: lowercase key words (grep), MUST/MUST NOT without actor or test, SHOULD without a stated exception, multi-obligation sentences, vague terms ('at once', 'as it works', 'ships', 'backoff', 'structured'), passive voice that hides the actor, and internal contradictions between requirements. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 characteristics were applied as named in this objective; the standard itself was not read (see the observation).

operational_learning.text: Check the requirements-language clause first: an RFC that adopts RFC 2119 without RFC 8174 makes every lowercase must, may and required ambiguous, so the count of lowercase key words is a quick measure of exposure.

Keep the defect table in a script that pulls each quoted line from disk and checks that each old text occurs exactly once on its stated line: line numbers and verbatim quotes are then verified, not remembered.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 cannot be read without purchase, and its ISO OBP preview requires accepting Terms of Use; a brief that asks for its wording should name a readable source or accept the characteristic names as given.

Most defects in this RFC are normative statements written without a key word ('the DB assigns', 'is reported at once', 'fold into'): searching for present-tense statements of behaviour in section 3 finds more defects than searching for key words.

proposals.what: line 100: - **RFC 2119.** The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY" and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119). -> - **Requirements language.** The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 ([RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119), [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. In lowercase, these words have their ordinary English meaning.
proposals.why: RFC 8174 section 2 (read 2026-11-16 at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174.txt): "The words have the meanings specified herein only when they are in all capitals." and "When these words are not capitalized, they have their normal English meanings and are not affected by this document." Its prescribed phrase includes "NOT RECOMMENDED" and cites BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174].
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: with the RFC 8174 phrase, a lowercase keyword is unambiguously ordinary English, so every remaining requirement must carry an uppercase keyword to bind.

proposals.what: line 153: Every entry of an item node is an item, and MUST carry these common fields: -> Every entry of an item node is an item. A writer MUST give every item each common field below, except a field marked OPTIONAL, a field marked REQUIRED under a condition that does not hold, and the fields a brief or an AAR inherits from `provenance` (second bullet below):
proposals.why: Requirements in one section must not contradict each other (29148 characteristic 'consistent', as named in the brief).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: the validator's `required` list follows from the corrected text without contradiction.

proposals.what: line 173: In a brief or an AAR, an item MAY omit `version`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `mission` and `created_at`; it inherits them from the document's `provenance`. -> In a brief or an AAR, an item MAY omit `version`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `mission` and `created_at`. A reader MUST then take `version` as 1, `created_at` from `provenance.created_at`, and `agent_id`, `agent_type` and `mission` from `provenance.written_by` (brief) or from `provenance.agent_id` and `provenance.mission`, with `agent_type` `delegate` (AAR).
proposals.why: A requirement must be complete: it must state every value a reader derives. The mapping removes the type clash between provenance.version and item version.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: 3.4.8's import of AAR items into the DB needs exactly this mapping.

proposals.what: line 187: 3.2.2. The type-specific fields are: -> 3.2.2. The type-specific fields are listed below. Every listed field is REQUIRED, except a field marked OPTIONAL and a field whose line states when it is present (for example `ref`, "once verified or falsified", and `answer`, "once answered"); a list field (`[]`) MAY be empty. The fields listed under "in an AAR or a running estimate" MUST NOT appear in a brief.
proposals.why: Each requirement must be verifiable; a field whose presence is unspecified cannot be checked. The session agent should then mark OPTIONAL any field it does not want required (for example how, when D874d-23's 'and/or' is applied).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: the schema writers in WP-1 would have one rule instead of guessing per field.

proposals.what: line 371: 3.3.7. A blocker the delegating agent already knows at launch MUST be written as a constraint or in the prompt body, and the objective it affects MUST say so. -> 3.3.7. When the delegating agent knows of a blocker at launch, it MUST state the blocker as a constraint or in the prompt body, and MUST name there each objective the blocker affects, by its `OBJ` id; it MUST NOT add to an objective's verbatim text (3.2.2).
proposals.why: Names the actor (passive 'be written' hid it) and removes the conflict with the verbatim rule.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: a delegating agent could not be led to edit a commander's verbatim objective.

proposals.what: line 385: - An objective that is not accomplished MUST cite the deviation that explains it. -> - An objective whose `status` is `partly` or `not accomplished` MUST cite in `deviation_refs` at least one deviation that explains the shortfall.
proposals.why: Uses the enum values literally (code font) so the requirement has one reading; aligned with 3.4.6.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: the validator and the delegate apply the same rule.

proposals.what: line 529: - no repo or worktree copy of `harness-db.py` may open a live session DB: tests and probes use throwaway DBs; -> - a repo or worktree copy of `harness-db.py` MUST NOT open a session DB under any `<repo>/.aitools/sessions/` directory; tests and probes MUST use throwaway DBs outside that directory;
proposals.why: RFC 2119 section 2: MUST NOT means 'an absolute prohibition'; 3.6.12 states a v4 helper crashes on a v5 DB, so the prohibition is safety-relevant. The directory makes the rule testable.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Yes: a reader could no longer read the line as a permission, and a probe could check the path it opens.

rfis.title: Do briefs/ changes go directly to main, like plans/?
rfis.question: RFC 0011 v1.3 3.3.1a (line 316) says a brief in the briefs directory is 'committed and pushed to `main`', but the CLAUDE.md 'Channel exception' lists only handoffs, relay.md, plans and CLAUDE.md as direct-to-main paths, and says 'Everything else uses a worktree and a PR.' Your order at L4045 was '45) add briefs to git, plans too.' Should `briefs/` be added to the Channel exception?
rfis.suggestion: Yes: add `briefs/` to the CLAUDE.md Channel exception, because a long-lifecycle brief changes at each launch (3.3.1a requires a new provenance version per launching session) and a PR per launch would cost your time; then 3.3.1a can keep 'pushed to main' as written in PRO for line 316.
